CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFREPORT

On Windows NT, CFREPORT runs a report designed in Crystal Reports (.rpt) against its data source and sends the result to the browser. Crystal Reports has no UNIX edition, so in KoldFusion the tag always raises an Application error.

Category

Extensibility

Syntax

<CFREPORT REPORT="report_path"
    ORDERBY="result_order"
    USERNAME="username"
    PASSWORD="password"
    FORMULA="formula">
  optional record selection formula
</CFREPORT>

Attributes

REPORT
Required. Path of the .rpt file.
ORDERBY
Optional. Sort order of the report records, overriding the report's own.
USERNAME
Optional. User name for the report's data source.
PASSWORD
Optional. Password for the report's data source.
FORMULA
Optional. One or more Crystal formulas, separated by semicolons, in the form name='value'.

Usage

Catch the error with CFTRY and build the report with CFQUERY and CFOUTPUT instead: grouped output (GROUP=) does most of what a banded report does.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFTRY>
  <CFREPORT REPORT="c:\reports\salaries.rpt" ORDERBY="Department">
  </CFREPORT>
  <CFCATCH TYPE="Application">
    <CFOUTPUT><P><I>#CFCATCH.Detail#</I> Here is a home-made report instead.</P></CFOUTPUT>
    <CFQUERY NAME="Pay" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets">
    SELECT Department, Salary FROM Employees ORDER BY Department
    </CFQUERY>
    <TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
    <TR BGCOLOR="#CCCCFF"><TH>Department</TH><TH>Staff</TH><TH>Payroll</TH></TR>
    <CFOUTPUT QUERY="Pay" GROUP="Department">
      <CFSET Total = 0><CFSET Staff = 0>
      <CFOUTPUT><CFSET Total = Total + Salary><CFSET Staff = Staff + 1></CFOUTPUT>
      <TR><TD>#Department#</TD><TD ALIGN=RIGHT>#Staff#</TD><TD ALIGN=RIGHT>#DollarFormat(Total)#</TD></TR>
    </CFOUTPUT>
    </TABLE>
  </CFCATCH>
</CFTRY>
